scope: Bounded independent static review of adaptive memory admission and its assembler integration. Separate relative-host lock exception is outside this review.

checked.finding: minimumReserveMB captures explicit RH_SYSTEM_RESERVE_MB before total-memory20% inflation; otherwise1024. preferredReserveMB keeps the original preferred policy. Worker estimate unchanged.

Fallback sets memoryPressureSeen, requires RAM stop success, then forces parallelMemorySnapshot(true). Missing refresh or insufficient free memory rejects. Later unknown snapshots cannot use original unknown-memory permission after pressure.

Only matching RAM stop request is written. Polling budget is5000ms. Live/unknown helper state rejects. Existing process record remains present; whole-run parallelShutdown and its completion fields are untouched.
workers1, effective floor and ramCapMB0 are assigned only after confirmed absence/exit and successful threshold check. HELD_BYTES is never added to free memory.
No promotion path resets workers after fallback. Thread share reads the updated workers1 before launching, and next while-condition prevents a second active task.
Idle denial check no longer depends on !progress. A cache-preparation progress flag cannot cause a second5000ms release attempt on the next scheduler iteration.
Accepted frozen restore returns before gate. Only a needed final compile/re-audit checks memory, before clearing new outputs or invoking Lean. Ordinary-worker barrier is checked.
Preferred/effective reserve + live warmer cap + (live+1)*worker estimate formula is preserved. Adaptive fallback is unavailable while a task is active.
memory_serial_fallback and ram_disabled_for_memory are booleans; preferred/effective reserve values are separate numeric MiB fields. Existing fields remain present.

Unique-site assertions and scoped replacements place the helper fragment once, preserve cache-only final return, and alter the intended scheduler denial condition. Assembler itself was inspected, not executed by this reviewer.

limitations: This is source inspection plus read-only byte/hash comparison, not execution of the JavaScript scheduler or any native tool.
The5000ms constant bounds the intended polling window; synchronous WSH property/I/O operations and scheduler latency have no hard real-time guarantee.
4096MiB is an admission estimate, not an enforced process memory cap; volatile memory can change after admission.
Existing initially-unknown memory serial policy is retained until known pressure is observed.
Run-plan JSON describes initial planning, while result metadata and fallback logs report effective serial degradation.
